sentences.zh: 那是约翰·弥尔顿在1652年写的一首十四行诗，旨在歌颂奥利弗·克伦威尔。当时距离查理一世被处决已经三年，而就在不久之后，令弥尔顿感到惊恐的是，

sentences.zh: 与我同在的是知名圆颅党人多米尼克·桑德布鲁克。

sentences.zh: 多米尼克。

sentences.zh: 谢谢你，汤姆。

sentences.zh: 你是他的粉丝吗？

sentences.zh: 我认为你可以把人分为克伦威尔派和非克伦威尔派。

sentences.zh: 我绝对是个克伦威尔派。

sentences.zh: 在我看来，汤姆，这是一个很大的论断，克伦威尔是我最喜欢的英国政治领袖，在我心里，他甚至比斯坦利·鲍德温和吉姆·卡拉汉还要好。

sentences.en: I think Cromwell is right up there, right at the top.
sentences.zh: 我认为克伦威尔绝对名列前茅，稳居巅峰。

sentences.en: I love Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 我爱克伦威尔。

sentences.en: I think he's so interesting, so interesting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他太有趣了，真的太有趣了。

sentences.en: Favourite in the sense that he's the most interesting British political figure, or favourite as in you admire his achievement.

sentences.en: I think, do you know what, both.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，我觉得两者兼有。

sentences.en: And I admire him for the fact he was in a position that no other Englishman has ever been in, other than Richard Cromwell, his son, being Lord Protector, having supreme power.
sentences.zh: 我钦佩他，是因为他处于一个从未有过其他英国人（除了他的儿子理查·克伦威尔）曾处于的位置，那就是担任护国公，拥有至高无上的权力。

sentences.en: And I think, by and large, you know, power reveals character, and I think it revealed him in a pretty good light, actually.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，总的来说，你知道，权力能揭示一个人的品格，我觉得权力把他展现得相当不错。

sentences.en: I think, you know, it didn't corrupt, particularly.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，你知道的，他并没有变得特别腐化。

sentences.en: He didn't behave especially badly.
sentences.zh: 他的表现也算不上多糟糕。

sentences.en: Now, I know Irish listeners are already, you know, throwing their phones across the room in fury.
sentences.zh: 现在我知道，爱尔兰听众大概已经愤怒得把手机扔向房间各处了。

sentences.en: But, by and large, I'm a big, big Cromwell fan.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，我是克伦威尔的超级大粉丝。

sentences.en: Okay, well, as you suggested, there are lots of people who would disagree with that verdict on Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 好吧，正如你所暗示的，有很多人并不同意对克伦威尔的这种评价。

sentences.en: I mean, he was the leader of one side in a civil war.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是内战中其中一派的领袖。

sentences.en: So, obviously, royalists, by and large, tend not to be keen on him.
sentences.zh: 所以很显然，保王党人总体来说往往不喜欢他。

sentences.en: And you mentioned Ireland, and in Ireland, his name is basically mud.

sentences.en: So, we need someone to guide us, I think, through the complexities and the ambivalences and the ambiguities,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们需要有人来引导我们，穿梭于那些复杂性、矛盾性与暧昧性之中，

sentences.en: not just of Cromwell's life, but of the period that we're particularly focusing on in this episode,
sentences.zh: 不仅是克伦威尔一生的复杂性，还有我们在这一集中特别关注的那段时期的复杂性，

sentences.en: which is, I guess you'd call it the British Republic, the period from Charles I's execution up to the restoration of his son, Charles II.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以称之为英国共和国时期，也就是从查理一世被处决到他的儿子查理二世复辟这段时期。

sentences.en: And there is no better person to provide us with that guidance than Paul Lay, who is editor of History Today,
sentences.zh: 没有人比保罗·莱伊更适合为我们提供这种指导了，他是《今日历史》杂志的编辑，

sentences.en: but also, more saliently for our purposes, author of a fabulous book, Providence Lost,
sentences.zh: 但对我们而言更重要的是，他是一本备受赞誉的精彩著作《失落的天堂：克伦威尔护国政权的兴衰》的作者。

sentences.en: The Rise and Fall of Cromwell's Protectorate, absolutely garlanded with praise.
sentences.zh: 保罗，非常感谢你能来参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: So, Paul, thanks so much for coming on and joining us.
sentences.zh: 你能帮我们理清一下吗，克伦威尔究竟是英雄还是狗熊？

sentences.en: And can you help us out, Cromwell, hero or zero?
sentences.zh: 嗯，两者都不是，当然。

sentences.en: Well, neither, of course.
sentences.zh: 我赞同多米尼克的看法，在某种程度上，他是最令人着迷的人物。

sentences.en: I agree with Dominic, to a certain extent, that he's the most fascinating character.
sentences.zh: 但同时——我想这也是让我觉得他更加迷人的地方——他极其难以捉摸。

sentences.en: But he's also, and I think this is what makes him even more fascinating for me, is that he's incredibly elusive.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是为什么这个人总能引发出种种神话传说。

sentences.en: And I think this is why the man lends himself to mythology.
sentences.zh: 关于克伦威尔，总是有太多需要脑补和填补的空白。

sentences.en: There's always an awful lot to fill in with Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在前三分之二的人生里，这个人几乎可以说是无名之辈，在历史记录中几乎不存在。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a man who's almost nothing for the first two thirds of his life, barely exists in the records.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间，在43岁时，他成为了——或者说他开始将自己塑造成英国历史上最伟大的骑兵指挥官之一，我们可以讨论他在其中的排名。

sentences.en: And then suddenly, at the age of 43, he becomes, or he sets out on a career as one of the great cavalry commanders in British history, and we can discuss where he ranks there.
sentences.zh: 但随后，正如多米尼克所说，他成为了一个几乎绝无仅有的独特人物。

sentences.en: But then he becomes this, as Dominic says, this almost unique figure.
sentences.zh: 我认为他是独一无二的，因为除了曾短暂担任过那个职位之外，理查根本无法与他相提并论。

sentences.en: And I think he is unique, because Richard is not remotely comparable, really, apart from the position he holds for a brief while.
sentences.zh: 他是这样一个独特的国家元首，他试图创造某种在我看来诞生于某种道德和神学努力的事物。

sentences.en: He is this unique head of state who tries to create something that I think is born of a kind of moral and theological endeavour.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这种政治遗产是具有延续性的。

sentences.en: And in some sense, the legacy is a continuous one.
sentences.zh: 君主制再也没有复辟，即使在复辟之后，也不是以前那种意义上的君主制了。

sentences.en: The monarchy never returns, even after the Restoration, in the sense that it was before that.
sentences.zh: 再也没有出现过类似查理一世个人统治那样的情况。

sentences.en: There's never a kind of Charles' personal rule or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，议会的权力开始占据上风。

sentences.en: Parliament becomes in the ascendant over that time.
sentences.zh: 当然，依然有许多问题需要去解决。

sentences.en: There are still things to be worked out.
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，他定义了我们。

sentences.en: Essentially, he does define us.
sentences.zh: 我认为他所进行的斗争、他所倡导的理念，至今仍引发共鸣。

sentences.en: And I think the battle that he waged, the ideas that he waged, are still resonant now.
sentences.zh: 我想到了T·S·艾略特的诗《小吉丁》（收录于《四首四重奏》中），他在诗中谈到国家内部和我们自身内部相互竞争的烈火与玫瑰，

sentences.en: And I think in particular of T.S.
sentences.zh: 通常我会有种类似吉尔伯特与沙利文台词的感觉，即世上所有的男孩和女孩，都有点自由主义倾向，或者都有点保守主义倾向。

sentences.en: Eliot's poem, Little Kidding, in The Four Quartets, when he talks about the fire and the rose that compete within the nation and compete within ourselves,
sentences.zh: 而这些正是在克伦威尔身上某种程度上能看到的斗争，也是在克伦威尔在其中发挥了重要塑造作用的国家里能看到的斗争。

sentences.en: often I think, like the Gilbert and Sullivan line, that every boy and girl alive is a little bit liberal or a little bit conservative.
sentences.zh: 但是保罗，难道最有趣的地方不正在于他并非只有一点点自由或一点点保守，而是双方都可以将他奉为自己人吗？正是这一点才让他如此迷人，

sentences.en: And those are the battles that we see in Cromwell to a certain extent, but in the nation that Cromwell was so important in forging.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上他囊括了所有英国政治，你不这么认为吗？

sentences.en: But Paul, isn't the interesting thing that he's not a little liberal or a little conservative, that either side can claim him, and that's what's so fascinating about him,
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为确实如此，因为左翼有很多人视他为英雄，仅仅是因为他们视他为共和国的捍卫者。

sentences.en: that he contains all, in a way, he contains all English politics, don't you think?
sentences.zh: 当然，右翼也有人视他为重要人物，因为他是一个英国民族主义者。

sentences.en: Yes, I think he does, because I think there's a lot of people on the left who regard him as heroic because they see him as a Republican for that alone.
sentences.zh: 他有着深刻的英国例外论思想。

sentences.en: And then there are, of course, people on the right who see him as important because he's an English nationaliSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为他也是宗教自由的捍卫者。

sentences.en: He has this profound idea of English exceptionalism.
sentences.zh: 当然，天主教徒肯定会对此反驳。

sentences.en: He is a defender of religious liberty, too, I think.
sentences.zh: 但就他对真正包容性宗教妥协方案的承诺而言，至少以17世纪中叶的标准来看，他是一个相当了不起的人物。

sentences.en: I mean, Catholics obviously would counter that.
sentences.zh: 而且他在作为英国军队的缔造者之一这一核心角色上，也常常被人遗忘。

sentences.en: But in terms of his commitment to a really quite capacious religious settlement, certainly by the standards of the mid-17th century, he's a pretty remarkable figure.
sentences.zh: 还有海军，对吧？

sentences.en: And he also has this central role as one of the creators of the British Army, too, where I think he's probably sometimes forgotten.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错，这很重要。

sentences.en: And the fleet, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 他曾拥有一艘名为“马斯顿荒原号”的战舰，我一直觉得这名字太酷了，我是从你的书里了解到的。

sentences.en: Yes, well, that's important.
sentences.zh: 是吗，以“荒原”命名的战舰可真不少呢，对吧？

sentences.en: He had a battleship called the Marston Moor, which I always thought was very cool, which I learned from your book.
sentences.zh: 并没有。

sentences.en: Yes, there are many battleships named after Moors, are there?
sentences.zh: 说实话，谈到马斯顿荒原之战，我突然觉得，也许对于那些对内战的各种战役并不是了如指掌的人来说，

sentences.en: No.

sentences.en: And actually, you know, talking about Marston Moor, it suddenly strikes me that perhaps for people who aren't entirely on top of all their various Civil War battles
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你最擅长这个了。

sentences.en: and so on, perhaps we should just set key things up before we get on to Cromwell himself and the Protectorate and everything.
sentences.zh: 你为什么不用30秒快速概括一下内战呢？

sentences.zh: 来吧。

sentences.zh: 谢谢你，汤姆。

sentences.en: Go on.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，汤姆。

sentences.en: Thank you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 好吧，上周我确实成功总结了《权力的游戏》，而且没有引发推特上的轩然大波。

sentences.en: Thank you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，英国内战可真是一个硬骨头。

sentences.zh: 这真的是英国内战吗？

sentences.en: So, well, the English Civil War is a tough one.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那完全是另一个问题了。

sentences.en: And is it the English Civil War?
sentences.zh: 好吧，保罗，请原谅我这么说。

sentences.zh: 所以基本上，当时你身处17世纪的英格兰或17世纪的英国。

sentences.en: OK, well, Paul, you have to forgive me for this.
sentences.zh: 查理一世一直在没有议会的情况下独揽大权。

sentences.en: So basically, you're in 17th century England or 17th century Britain.
sentences.zh: 他似乎有点自视甚高，把自己当成了一个绝对君主。

sentences.zh: 但在17世纪30年代末，所有事情一下子都出了岔子。

sentences.en: He slightly sort of seems to fancy himself as an absolute monarch.

sentences.en: But at the end of the 1630s, everything kind of goes wrong at once.

sentences.en: At the same time, there is a rebellion or a war breaks out with the Scots over a prayer book that Charles is trying to impose.
sentences.zh: 对苏格兰的战争打得非常糟糕。

sentences.en: So two of these three kingdoms are, as it were, in revolt.
sentences.zh: 查理需要更多的资金。

sentences.en: The war goes very bad against the Scots.
sentences.zh: 而他筹集资金的唯一方法就是重新召集议会。

sentences.en: Charles needs more money.
sentences.zh: 但议会并不喜欢他。

sentences.zh: 双方陷入了僵局。

sentences.zh: 他竖起军旗，号召人们团结在他身边对抗议会。

sentences.zh: 于是，国王与议会之间爆发了内战。

sentences.zh: 所以你面临的就是这样一场多方交织的内战。

sentences.zh: 长话短说，第一次内战对查理来说非常糟糕。

sentences.en: So you've got this sort of multifaceted civil war.
sentences.zh: 他战败了。

sentences.en: Now, to cut a very long story short, the first civil war goes very badly for Charles.
sentences.zh: 但在那个时候，议会派并不想杀他，也不想把他赶下台或者别的什么。

sentences.en: He loses.
sentences.zh: 他们信仰君主制。

sentences.zh: 所以在和查理进行谈判。

sentences.zh: 他们把他软禁起来，试图与他达成妥协。

sentences.zh: 而且他们以为自己快要谈妥了。

sentences.en: They've got him kind of locked up and they're trying to get a deal with him.
sentences.zh: 但查理却背着他们搞小动作。

sentences.en: And they think they're going to get a deal.
sentences.zh: 他与苏格兰人秘密达成了一项协议。

sentences.zh: 苏格兰人大举南下对抗议会派。

sentences.en: So one of his three kingdoms, but the sort of his old enemy, as it were.
sentences.zh: 于是爆发了第二次内战。

sentences.en: And there's now a second civil war.
sentences.zh: 嗯，第二次内战。

sentences.en: So this incredibly complicated story has taken this Game of Thrones style twiSt.
sentences.zh: 但由于拥有了新模范军（其领军人物正是奥利弗·克伦威尔），议会最终也赢得了这场内战。

sentences.en: Well, the second civil war.
sentences.zh: 既然他们已经赢了两场内战，

sentences.zh: 由于他们认定自己无法与查理达成任何协议，因为事实证明他完全不可信。

sentences.en: So now they've won two civil wars.
sentences.zh: 正如他们所称的那样，他是血腥之人、国家的叛徒、背叛了人民的敌基督的代理人。

sentences.en: Because they've decided that they can't do any sort of deal with Charles because he's proved himself utterly untrustworthy.
sentences.zh: 所以他必须被清除。

sentences.zh: 于是他们决定砍掉他的脑袋。

sentences.en: So they decide to cut his head off.
sentences.zh: 人头落地。

sentences.zh: 这就引发了一个问题：接下来我们到底该怎么办？

sentences.en: They're actually not.
sentences.zh: 但实际上并非如此。

sentences.en: Most of them are decided by the Council of State, which, along with Cromwell, is basically running things at this point.
sentences.zh: 他们大多由国务委员会决定，该委员会与克伦威尔一起基本上在此时管理着一切。

sentences.en: And it's by no means as mad in terms of the practices, as you might think from the way it's modelled on the Old Testament Sanhedrin.
sentences.zh: 从其实践来看，它并不像你从它模仿旧约公议会的运作方式所想象的那样疯狂。

sentences.en: It puts through quite a few reforms of the law that are much needed.
sentences.zh: 它通过了相当多的急需的法律改革。

sentences.en: There's always quite a few lawyers around the parliamentary side.
sentences.zh: 议会派周围总是有相当多的律师。

sentences.en: But it rubs up against the army.
sentences.zh: 但它与军队发生了冲突。

sentences.en: And here is the rub, because everything in the end that takes place during this decade is ultimately dependent upon the power of the army.
sentences.zh: 问题就在这里，因为在这个十年中发生的每一件事最终都依赖于军队的力量。

sentences.en: If the army doesn't want it, it doesn't really happen.
sentences.zh: 如果军队不想要它，它就不会真正发生。

sentences.en: And Cromwell is the significant figure because he's the person who has the kind of trust or enough trust on both sides for them to invest in with the prominence he has at this point.
sentences.zh: 克伦威尔是一个重要人物，因为他是那种在双方都拥有信任或足够信任的人，以便他们将他推到此时的显赫地位。

sentences.en: However, the nominated assembly does fail because it doesn't give enough money to the army.
sentences.zh: 然而，提名议会确实失败了，因为它没有给军队足够的资金。

sentences.en: And this is a common theme throughout this period.
sentences.zh: 这是贯穿这一时期的常见主题。

sentences.en: And so another figure emerges instead of Thomas Harrison, who disappears to the margins here.
sentences.zh: 因此，另一位人物取代了退居幕后的托马斯·哈里森脱颖而出。

sentences.en: And the person who emerges is the figure who's very much seen at this point.
sentences.zh: 而脱颖而出并被高度关注的那个人，

sentences.en: And we're talking about 1653, 54 here, who is John Lambert, who has had a military career almost as spectacular as Cromwell's,
sentences.zh: 我们这里指的是1653、54年，他就是约翰·兰伯特，他的军事生涯几乎和克伦威尔一样辉煌，

sentences.en: who spends most of the time while the nominated assembly is bickering, coming up with the world's first written constitution, which is the instrument of government.
sentences.zh: 他在提名议会争吵不休的大部分时间里，都在起草世界上第一部成文宪法，即《政府管理法》（Instrument of Government）。

sentences.en: And what that does, among many other things, is reconfigure the trinity of king, lords and commons into a new trinity, holy or not, of protector,
sentences.zh: 这样做带来的众多结果之一，就是将国王、上议院和下议院的三位一体重组为一个新的三位一体——不管是否神圣——即护国公，

sentences.en: which is the position that will be offered to Cromwell, knowing that he's unlikely to take the crown.
sentences.zh: 这将是提供给克伦威尔的职位，因为人们知道他不太可能接受王位。

sentences.en: And you have, instead of the lords, a council of state with people like Lambert around him, the great and good of the regime.
sentences.zh: 除了上议院，你还有一个由兰伯特等人组成的国务委员会，他们是政权的精英和中坚力量。

sentences.en: And then you have parliament, which is pretty denuded by this point.
sentences.zh: 然后你有了到此时已经被大大削弱的议会。

sentences.en: So that's the settlement to which Cromwell agrees.
sentences.zh: 这就是克伦威尔同意的政治妥协。

sentences.en: And that is when the protectorate begins.
sentences.zh: 护国公时期也由此开始。

sentences.en: And is it fair to talk of Cromwell there as a dictator?
sentences.zh: 把那时的克伦威尔称为独战者（独裁者）公平吗？

sentences.en: Is that too strong?
sentences.zh: 这会不会太夸张了？

sentences.en: I know people did talk at the turn of the 20th century, looking abroad, they thought, oh, Cromwell was a sort of prototype for modern dictators.
sentences.zh: 我知道人们在20世纪之交时曾谈论过，放眼海外，他们会想，哦，克伦威尔是现代独裁者的某种原型。

sentences.en: But do you think that's wrong?
sentences.zh: 但你认为这不对吗？

sentences.en: Or do you think he is a military strong man in a sort of recognisably modern mould?
sentences.zh: 或者你认为他只是一个以某种可识别的现代模式存在的军事强人？

sentences.en: No, I don't think he is.
sentences.zh: 不，我不认为他是。

sentences.en: I mean, you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你完全说得对。

sentences.en: It was a common analogy with the dictator of the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 这与20世纪30年代的独裁者是一个常见的类比。

sentences.en: And in fact, it was one made by, among other people, C.V.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这也是由其他人提出的，比如C.V.

sentences.en: Wedgwood, who was a great historian of this period, who recanted very publicly at a meeting of the Cromwell Association many decades later, and said she was completely wrong.
sentences.zh: 韦奇伍德（C.V. Wedgwood），他是研究这一时期的伟大历史学家，几十年后她在克伦威尔协会的一次会议上公开忏悔，并表示自己完全错了。

sentences.en: It's very difficult to argue.
sentences.zh: 这很难辩解。

sentences.en: One, because whatever is false, Cromwell does continuously seek a settlement and constantly refers to the idea of healing and settling, which I think is sincere.
sentences.zh: 第一，无论事实如何，克伦威尔确实一直在寻求一种妥协，并不断提到治愈和和解的理念，我认为这是真诚的。

sentences.en: The way he goes about it is not always sincere, hence Blair Worden's wonderful phrase about Cromwell being practised of not knowing.
sentences.zh: 他行事的方式并不总是真诚的，因此布莱尔·沃登（Blair Worden）有一句精彩的名言，形容克伦威尔精于“装作不知”。

sentences.en: So there's definitely this slippery side to him that can be absent when things happen, despite his hand, his fingerprints being all over them.
sentences.zh: 所以他身上确实有这种狡猾的一面，当事情发生时，尽管他的手笔和指纹无处不在，他却可以置身事外。

sentences.en: But military dictator, even if the desire is there, and I don't think it is, there is not the means of anything like a military dictatorship in a 17th century European state.
sentences.zh: 但军事独裁者——即便真有这种意愿，而我认为并没有——在17世纪的欧洲国家中，也根本不具备建立类似军事独裁的手段。

sentences.en: I mean, justice and there, the communications and the technologies, the kind of surveillance that you need.
sentences.zh: 我是说，正义之类的事情，还有通讯与技术，以及你需要的那种监视。

sentences.en: It's just not possible.
sentences.zh: 这根本是不可能的。

sentences.en: So, Paul, basically, the protectorate is a kind of protracted exercise in trying to work out a framework that will enable England, and indeed Britain, I mean,
sentences.zh: 所以，保罗，基本上，护国公时期是一场旷日持久的实践，旨在摸索出一套框架，让英格兰，乃至整个不列颠——我是说，

sentences.en: because it's for the whole of Great Britain, isn't it, for the first time, to function, but also to put down solid foundations.
sentences.zh: 因为这是第一次，为了整个大不列颠的利益而运作，不仅仅是为了运转，也是为了奠定坚实的基础。

sentences.en: And in the long run, that is what dooms the British Republic, is that the foundations are inadequate, basically, to cope with Cromwell's death.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，正是这一点注定了不列颠共和国的命运，因为这些基础基本上不足以应付克伦威尔的去世。

sentences.en: And so after Cromwell's death, we've got a question here from Matthew Butcher.
sentences.zh: 所以在克伦威尔去世后，我们这里有一个来自马修·布彻的问题。

sentences.en: Was the restoration inevitable, or is there a realistic path which keeps England as a republic?
sentences.zh: 复辟是不可避免的，还是存在一条让英格兰保持共和国体制的现实路径？

sentences.en: Well, it wasn't a republic.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它其实算不上一个共和国。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that's part of the problem.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这正是问题的一部分。

sentences.en: When Cromwell's death, it's not a republic.
sentences.zh: 在克伦威尔去世时，它并不是一个共和国。

sentences.en: It's a protectorate.
sentences.zh: 它是一个护国公时期。

sentences.en: It's a quasi-monarchy.
sentences.zh: 它是一种准君主制。

sentences.en: It's something akin, maybe, to a kind of Venetian settlement.
sentences.zh: 它或许有点类似于某种威尼斯式的政治安排。

sentences.en: And people like James Harrington, who wrote Oceana as an advice book to Cromwell, were obsessed by classical republicanism and Venetian republicanism,
sentences.zh: 像詹姆斯·哈灵顿这样的人——他写了《大洋洲记》作为献给克伦威尔的建议书——他们痴迷于古典共和主义和威尼斯共和主义，

sentences.en: as was Milton and this idea of an elected doge, an elected protector, which was always an option.
sentences.zh: 弥尔顿也是如此，他们怀有选举产生总督、选举产生护国公的想法，这始终是一个备选项。

sentences.en: But I'm afraid that the entire population was never really convinced of an alternative to a monarchy.
sentences.zh: 但我恐怕全体民众从来没有真正信服过君主制之外的替代方案。

sentences.en: The old bottom, the ancient constitution, is constantly referred to by people in parliament when they refer to the Norman yoke, for example,
sentences.zh: 议会中的人们在提到诸如诺曼枷锁之类的概念时，总是会搬出古老的底层、古代宪政，

sentences.en: and the ancient constitution, but to most people's minds, even many of those in parliament, the ancient constitution is the monarchy and the commons and the House of Lords.
sentences.zh: 以及古代宪政，但在大多数人的心目中，甚至在许多议会成员的心目中，古代宪政就是君主制、平民院和上议院。

sentences.en: That's the way it works.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样运作的。

sentences.en: And we simply have this interregnum where an alternative is attempted.
sentences.zh: 我们只是经历了一段尝试替代方案的空位期。

sentences.en: But I think there's, and I think this is interesting about Cromwell here, is that as a military figure, he's incredibly decisive.
sentences.zh: 但我认为——关于克伦威尔，我觉得有趣的一点是，作为一个军事人物，他极其果断。

sentences.en: When you read the records of his actions of Naseby, for example, this is a decisive figure when you look at him in his battles.
sentences.zh: 当你阅读他关于纳斯比战役等行动的记录时，你会发现，当你在战场上审视他时，这是一个极为果断的人物。

sentences.en: But I think as a political figure, he's never really sure what the settlement should be.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，作为一个政治人物，他从来不确定最终的政治安排应该是什么。

sentences.en: And he's offered various settlements, particularly by people who emerge towards the end of the protectorate, or at least towards the end of his life,
sentences.zh: 而且人们提出了各种政治安排，特别是那些在护国公时期末期、或者说在他生命接近终点时出现的人，

sentences.en: who are very concerned to find the settlement.
sentences.zh: 他们非常热切地想要找到一个政治安排。

sentences.en: They know that this is a man in his late 50s, he's wracked by various illnesses, he's had a tough military life, as well as the stresses of this new kind of government.
sentences.zh: 他们知道这是一个年近五十岁的人，饱受各种疾病折磨，有着艰难的军旅生涯，还要承受这种新型政府带来的压力。

sentences.en: And he's not going to be around forever, and probably not much longer.
sentences.zh: 他不会永远活下去，可能也活不了太久了。

sentences.en: And so a settlement has to be found.
sentences.zh: 因此必须找到一个政治安排。

sentences.en: And I think there are basically four alternatives that are presented to him.
sentences.zh: 我认为基本上有四个替代方案摆在他面前。

sentences.en: The first is that he just accepts kingship.
sentences.zh: 第一个是他直接接受王位。

sentences.en: He becomes Oliver I, and that becomes an hereditary position.
sentences.zh: 他成为奥利弗一世，而且这是一个世袭职位。

sentences.en: To the House of Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 传给克伦威尔家族。

sentences.en: So the House of Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 也就是克伦威尔家族。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But there's also the one where he accepts kingship, Oliver I, but that is not hereditary.
sentences.zh: 但还有一种方案是他接受王位、成为奥利弗一世，但这并非世袭。

sentences.en: It's an elective kingship, rather like Venice.
sentences.zh: 这是一种选举产生的王位，非常类似于威尼斯。

sentences.en: The same for the protector.
sentences.zh: 护国公也是如此。

sentences.en: You could take on this title of protector and continue it and make that hereditary, or again, elective.
sentences.zh: 你可以担任这个护国公的头衔并延续下去，让它成为世袭的，或者同样由选举产生。

sentences.en: And the truth is that at the end, when he's on his deathbed during that great storm on the 3rd of September 1658,
sentences.zh: 事实是，在最后，当他在1658年9月3日那场大风暴中临终时，

sentences.en: and says the settlement is that it will be the position of Lord Protector will pass on to Richard.
sentences.zh: 并表示这一安排是让护国公的职位传给理查德。

sentences.en: So essentially, the choice is a Lord Protector of an hereditary nature, but that's the position that we are.
sentences.zh: 所以从本质上讲，选择是一个世袭性质的护国公，但这就是我们所处的位置。

sentences.en: And so by the time Cromwell dies, the settlement, the succession has not been decided on.
sentences.zh: 因此，到克伦威尔去世时，政治安排和权力继承尚未敲定。

sentences.en: In many ways, that's quite reminiscent of what happened with Cromwell's own hero, Elizabeth I, when you have a great deal of uncertainty as to how you settle succession.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，这很让人想起克伦威尔自己的偶像伊丽莎白一世的情况，当时对于如何解决继承问题存在着极大的不确定性。

sentences.en: And so Richard briefly serves as Lord Protector.
sentences.zh: 因此，理查德短暂地担任了护国公。

sentences.en: He's not really on for it.
sentences.zh: 他其实并不太乐意干这个。

sentences.en: There's kind of general meltdown and people basically decided, well, if we're going to have a monarchical system,
sentences.zh: 局势基本上全面崩盘，人们基本上认为，好吧，既然我们要搞君主制系统，

sentences.en: we might as well get the original Stuart family back and Charles II returns.
sentences.zh: 还不如把原来的斯图亚特家族请回来，于是查理二世回来了。

sentences.en: So we've had a very nifty gallop through the history of the Protectorate and building up to that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们非常轻快地纵览了护国公时期的历史以及在此之前的积淀。

sentences.en: I think it's worth saying, sorry, that in terms of Richard, it's not a question of whether Richard's up for it or not.
sentences.zh: 我认为有必要说一句，抱歉，就理查德而言，这并不是理查德愿不愿意接受的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't get the sense that he is, although he's incredibly long lived.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不觉得他愿意，尽管他极其长寿。

sentences.en: So that would have been good.
sentences.zh: 那倒挺不错的。

sentences.en: He lives well into the 18th century.
sentences.zh: 他一直活到了18世纪。

sentences.en: But I think the fundamental goes back to what I said earlier.
sentences.zh: 但我认为根本问题还是要回到我刚才说过的话上。

sentences.en: He hasn't got the support of the army.
sentences.zh: 他没有军队的支持。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: That's the point.
sentences.zh: 这就是关键所在。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So and on the theme of the role that the army plays, that's something perhaps that we can come back to.
sentences.zh: 所以，顺着军队所扮演的角色这个主题，这也许是我们接下来可以回过头来探讨的话题。

sentences.en: We should come back to look at Cromwell's relationship with the radicals, the levellers, which is also kind of key theme.
sentences.zh: 我们应该回过头来审视克伦威尔与激进派、平民派的关系，这也是一个核心主题。

sentences.en: And we must come and look at his role in Ireland as well.
sentences.zh: 而且我们必须来看看他在爱尔兰所扮演的角色。

sentences.en: But I think for now, we should quickly go to a commercial break.
sentences.zh: 但我想目前我们应该迅速进入一个商业广告时间。

sentences.en: And when we come back, we'll look at Cromwellian controversies.
sentences.zh: 等我们回来后，我们将探讨关于克伦威尔的争议。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史其余部分》节目。

sentences.en: We are debating the good old cause of the 17th century, the life and times of Oliver Cromwell, the fortunes of the British Republic, with me, top roundhead Dominic Sandbrook,
sentences.zh: 我们正在讨论17世纪那个美好的伟大事业、奥利弗·克伦威尔的生平与时代、不列颠共和国的沉浮，陪伴我的有坚定的保皇派（圆颅党）多米尼克·桑德布鲁克，

sentences.en: foppish cavalier Tom Holland and actual Cromwellian expert who knows what he's talking about, Paul Lay.
sentences.zh: 衣着华丽的骑士党汤姆·霍兰，以及真正的克伦威尔专家、对此了如指掌的保罗·莱伊。

sentences.en: So, Paul, can I kick off with a question?
sentences.zh: 那么，保罗，我能以一个问题开场吗？

sentences.en: We were just talking about the course of the protectorates and the sort of the whole story of the 1650s before the break.
sentences.zh: 我们在中场休息前刚刚讨论了护国公时期的历程以及1650年代的整个故事。

sentences.en: So when people like sort of Tony Benn, Labour politician, or sort of generally sort of left wing people say this was a missed opportunity for republicanism,
sentences.zh: 所以，当诸如托尼·本恩这样的工党政治家，或者一般意义上的左翼人士说这是一次错失的共和主义良机时，

sentences.en: are they basically wrong?
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是错了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, from your last stuff, it sounded like you thought there was never really a possibility of a genuinely sort of vaguely democratic republic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从你刚才的言论听来，你似乎认为根本不存在真正意义上、隐约具有民主色彩的共和国的可能性。

sentences.en: It was always going to be a monarchical solution one way or the other.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，这终究会走向一种君主制的解决方案。

sentences.en: Well, I don't think it's inevitable.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不认为这是不可避免的。

sentences.en: But the people like Tony Benn, there are many historians, very good historians, identify with the Levellers.
sentences.zh: 但像托尼·本恩这样的人，还有许多历史学家，非常优秀的历史学家，都认同平民派。

sentences.en: Indeed, in my paperback version of the book, there is a picture of me in Burford Graveyard.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在我那本书的平装版里，就有一张我在伯福德墓地的照片。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, I know it well, Burford Graveyard.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，我很熟悉，伯福德墓地。

sentences.en: With the three troopers there.
sentences.zh: 里面有那三名骑兵。

sentences.en: And Dominic, just to interrupt, another of your quick resumes, who are the Levellers?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，打断一下，用你那简短的风格再总结一下，平民派究竟是谁？

sentences.en: Oh, golly.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: OK, so the Levellers, they are soldiers in the new model army.
sentences.zh: 好吧，平民派，他们是新模范军中的士兵。

sentences.en: They've been basically told they've got to go to Ireland.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上被告知必须去爱尔兰。

sentences.en: They don't want to go.
sentences.zh: 他们不想去。

sentences.en: But also they're kind of on the, as it were, the left wing of that movement.
sentences.zh: 但同时他们也处于那个运动的左翼，可以说是这样。

sentences.en: They are much more democratic.
sentences.zh: 他们要民主得多。

sentences.en: They want to sort of, they want to get a vote.
sentences.zh: 他们想要争取投票权。

sentences.en: They want a more, what we would recognise as a more sort of democratic republican settlement.
sentences.zh: 他们想要一种我们所认识的、更具民主共和色彩的政治安排。

sentences.en: Cromwell is Blair and the Levellers are the Corbynites.
sentences.zh: 克伦威尔就像是布莱尔，而平民派就像是科尔宾派。

sentences.en: I wouldn't go that far.
sentences.zh: 我不会走得那么远。

sentences.en: These analogies are very, very difficult.
sentences.zh: 这些类比非常非常困难。

sentences.en: The Levellers believing something like they are building a new Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 平民派坚信的事情类似于他们正在建设一个新的耶路撒冷。

sentences.en: And that's the kind of language that has been a part of an English radical tradition ever since, if not before.
sentences.zh: 这种语言自那时起（甚至在此之前）就一直是英国激进传统的一部分。

sentences.en: And Tony Benn would appeal to that.
sentences.zh: 而托尼·本恩会呼吁这种精神。

sentences.en: And it's a real tradition.
sentences.zh: 这是一个真正的传统。

sentences.en: And Cromwell, to people like Benn, is a kind of problematic figure, right?
sentences.zh: 对于本恩这样的人来说，克伦威尔是一个颇具争议的人物，对吧？

sentences.en: Because he's a villain to Benn.
sentences.zh: 因为在本恩眼里他是个恶棍。

sentences.en: Tony Benn said that Dennis Healy was the Cromwell of the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 托尼·本恩曾说丹尼斯·希利是20世纪70年代的克伦威尔。

sentences.en: Yes, and in many ways, I'd say Dennis Healy is the far more attractive figure, but certainly the more cultivated figure.
sentences.zh: 是的，在许多方面，我会说丹尼斯·希利是一个更有吸引力的人物，但绝对是一个更有文化素养的人物。

sentences.en: And certainly, actually, the more effective political figure.
sentences.zh: 而且当然，实际上也是一个更有效的政治人物。

sentences.en: But we can debate that at some other time.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以改天再来讨论这个。

sentences.en: And in 1650, so a year after Charles I's death, Cromwell is getting ready to cross to Ireland.
sentences.zh: 在1650年——也就是查理一世死后的一年，克伦威尔正准备渡海去爱尔兰。

sentences.en: And the army is camped at Burford.
sentences.zh: 军队当时驻扎在伯福德。

sentences.en: And there is essentially this kind of mutiny, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 基本上发生了一场兵变，对吧？

sentences.en: It is a mutiny, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这确实是一场兵变，不是吗？

sentences.en: They're in the church, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 他们当时在教堂里，对吧？

sentences.en: They're all in the church.
sentences.zh: 他们全在教堂里。

sentences.en: And what does Cromwell do?
sentences.zh: 克伦威尔做了什么？

sentences.en: Well, he takes three of them out and he shoots them against the wall of Burford Church.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他把其中三个人带出来，在伯福德教堂的墙边把他们枪决了。

sentences.en: And yes, and there's a kind of memorial to them, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 是的，那里有一个关于他们的纪念碑，对吧？

sentences.en: There is, yes.
sentences.zh: 确实有。

sentences.en: And it's an interesting memorial because we talk about Cromwell being all things to all men.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的纪念碑，因为我们常说克伦威尔对所有人而言扮演着各种不同的角色。

sentences.en: Because it's not just Tony Benn who finds Burford, this place of pilgrimage.
sentences.zh: 因为不仅托尼·本恩视伯福德为朝圣之地，

sentences.en: It's also a place where conservative Brexiteers such as Daniel Hannan eulogise as this birthplace of the free-born English man,
sentences.zh: 保守派脱欧派人士如丹尼尔·汉南也将其歌颂为自由出生的英国人的发源地，

sentences.en: which, of course, is the phrase we associate with the most famous of all the levelers.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也是我们与所有平民派中最著名的人物联系在一起的短语。

sentences.en: So it's funny that we say that because I don't necessarily see this idea of free-born English man being a kind of right or left-wing thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我们这样说很有趣，因为我不认为“自由出生的英国人”这个概念必然带有左翼或右翼的色彩。

sentences.en: It can appeal to both sides.
sentences.zh: 它可以吸引双方。

sentences.en: Again, we're back to that theme of the fire and the road.
sentences.zh: 我们又回到了那个烈火与道路的主题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so at Burford, essentially, the mutiny gets put down.
sentences.zh: 所以在伯福德，兵变基本上被平息了。

sentences.en: And one of the things that the levelers are objecting to is the very idea of crossing to Ireland.
sentences.zh: 平民派反对的事项之一，正是渡海前往爱尔兰这个想法本身。

sentences.en: So there's a leveler leaflet that's distributed to the New Model Army on the eve of the crossing to Ireland.
sentences.zh: 因此，在渡海前往爱尔兰的前夕，新模范军中散发了一份平民派的传单。

sentences.en: It says, whether Julius Caesar, Alexander the Great, William Duke of Normandy, or any other, the great conquerors of the world,
sentences.zh: 上面写着，无论是尤利乌斯·恺撒、亚历山大大帝、诺曼底公爵威廉，还是任何其他世界的伟大征服者，

sentences.en: were any other than so many great and lawless thieves, which is a kind of very – I mean, that really is a radical idea, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 他们与那些大大小小的无赖强盗有什么区别呢？这真是一种——我的意思是，这真的是一个激进的想法，不是吗？

sentences.en: That the whole – the foundational idea for the crossing to Ireland is presumably for Cromwell that God wants him to do it, that the Irish rebels are – no, you're –
sentences.zh: 整个——渡征爱尔兰的基础理念，对于克伦威尔来说，大概是因为上帝希望他这么做，爱尔兰叛军是——不，你——

sentences.en: There is that.
sentences.zh: 确实有这种说法。

sentences.en: People always ask me what it's comparable to.
sentences.zh: 人们总是问我这可以和什么相比。

sentences.en: There are certain parallels of the conquest of Ireland that does take place under Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 克伦威尔统治下对爱尔兰的征服，确实有着某些相似之处。

sentences.en: And preceded Cromwell and happened long after Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 这种征服在克伦威尔之前发生过，在克伦威尔很久之后也发生过。

sentences.en: And comparisons have been drawn by some historians, British historians, comparing it to Nazi atrocities
sentences.zh: 一些历史学家、英国历史学家将其与纳粹暴行进行了比较，

sentences.en: or what happened on the Eastern Front during the Second World War, these kind of comparisons there of genocide.
sentences.zh: 或者将其与第二次世界大战期间东线发生的事情进行比较，这其中存在着关于种族灭绝的类比。

sentences.en: What I think it's most like, most comparable to, as a historic event, and I think this is what the levellers recognised and the critics of it recognised, is the Norman conqueSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为它最像、作为历史事件最可比的——而且我认为平民派和它的批评者们都意识到了这一点——是诺曼征服。

sentences.en: The levellers and people around them talk about the Norman yoke.
sentences.zh: 平民派及其周围的人谈论诺曼枷锁。

sentences.en: They talk about the ancient constitution.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论古代宪政。

sentences.en: That bit I just quoted mentions William.
sentences.zh: 我刚才引用的那段话提到了威廉。

sentences.en: I mean, that's what the illusion is too.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是典故所指的方向。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And what happens, what turns out, is wholly akin to the Norman conquest, whereby – this is attempted in Scotland as well – but far,
sentences.zh: 结果证明，这与诺曼征服完全相似，由此——苏格兰也曾尝试过这一点——但在爱尔兰，

sentences.en: far more perniciously and aggressively in Ireland – is the anglicisation of these islands, of the islands of Britain and Ireland, but to make them entirely English.
sentences.zh: 其手段要阴险和激进得多——那就是将这些岛屿、将不列颠和爱尔兰岛屿英格化，使其变得完全英国化。

sentences.en: And the ideology behind that, I suspect, is that – and this goes back to people like Harrison, but I think it's something that Cromwell believes too, and those around him –
sentences.zh: 我认为其背后的意识形态是——这可以追溯到像哈灵顿这样的人，但我认为这也是克伦威尔以及他周围的人所坚信的——

sentences.en: is that the English are an elect nation.
sentences.zh: 那就是英国人是一个天选之国。

sentences.en: Just as Israel was the elect nation of the Old Testament, England is the elect nation of the New.
sentences.zh: 正如以色列是旧约中的天选之国一样，英格兰是新约中的天选之国。

sentences.en: So Cromwell is like Joshua leading the Israelites into the Promised Land.
sentences.zh: 所以克伦威尔就像带领以色列人进入应许之地的约书亚。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of that – that's what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有点像那种——这就是我们所谈论的。

sentences.en: And he certainly refers to such allusions.
sentences.zh: 而且他确实经常提到这样的典故。

sentences.en: So we've had a host of questions, as you can imagine, about Cromwell, his role in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 正如你可以想象的那样，我们收到了大量关于克伦威尔及其在爱尔兰所扮演角色的问题。

sentences.en: So we've got Seamus MacArthur.
sentences.zh: 所以我们请到了谢默斯·麦克阿瑟。

sentences.en: As a Northern Irishman, we often hear of Cromwell's brutality against the Irish.
sentences.zh: 作为一个北爱尔兰人，我们经常听到克伦威尔对爱尔兰人的残暴行径。

sentences.en: How much of this is true?
sentences.zh: 其中有多少是真的？

sentences.en: How much is it exaggerated?
sentences.zh: 有多少被夸大了？

sentences.en: What was the source of this animosity?
sentences.zh: 这种敌意的根源是什么？

sentences.en: Was it a straightforward religious drive against Catholic Irish?
sentences.zh: 这是否是一场针对天主教爱尔兰人的直接宗教迫害？

sentences.en: We've got Luke Hennessy with no shortage of other available candidates.
sentences.zh: 我们请来了卢克·亨内西，同时也有不少其他候选人。

sentences.en: Why has a very special place in Irish hell been reserved for Cromwell for so long if the atrocities were exaggerated?
sentences.zh: 如果暴行被夸大了，为什么爱尔兰地狱里有一个如此特殊的座位，给克伦威尔留了这么久？

sentences.en: Okay, I mean, so were the atrocities exaggerated?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，那么这些暴行真的被夸大了吗？

sentences.en: If there were atrocities, what was Cromwell's role in it?
sentences.zh: 如果真有暴行，克伦威尔在其中扮演了什么角色？

sentences.en: Is the black tones in which Ireland tends to paint Cromwell justified?
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰人往往把克伦威尔描绘得十恶不赦，这种灰暗的基调真的合理吗？

sentences.en: If not, why is he seen as such a kind of a diabolic figure?
sentences.zh: 如果没有，为什么他会被视为这样一个恶魔般的人物？

sentences.en: This is quite a question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当深刻的问题。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉。

sentences.en: No pressure.
sentences.zh: 不用有压力。

sentences.en: What I tend to think about this is that I don't know whether you've been to Cromwell's house in Ely, in which he spent – in the 800 years that the house has been built,
sentences.zh: 我对这件事的看法是——我不知道你有没有去过克伦威尔在伊利的故居，在这栋建筑存在的那八百年里，

sentences.en: he spent 20 years connected to it, not even living there, but it is Cromwell's house.
sentences.zh: 他在那里度过了20年，甚至都没有真正住在那里，但那就是克伦威尔的故居。

sentences.en: And I think there's a kind of analogy there with Cromwell in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 我想这和克伦威尔在爱尔兰的情况有某种类比。

sentences.en: Cromwell spent about nine months in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 克伦威尔在爱尔兰呆了大约九个月。

sentences.en: His actions were decisive, sometimes I would argue barbaric, particularly in his treatment of Catholic priests in court blood.
sentences.zh: 他的行动是果断的，有时我认为甚至是野蛮的，特别是他在法庭血案中对待天主教神职人员的方式。

sentences.en: But the facts have often been mythologised, as Cromwell has been.
sentences.zh: 但事实往往被神话化了，克伦威尔本人也是如此。

sentences.en: And I don't think – there was one question from one person on Twitter, I noticed, who said, why is Cromwell celebrated in England but not in Ireland?
sentences.zh: 我不认为——我注意到推特上有一个人提问说，为什么克伦威尔在英国受到赞誉，而在爱尔兰却没有？

sentences.en: And I thought, he's not celebrated in England.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，他在英国根本没有受到赞誉。

sentences.en: He's almost as controversial character in England as he is in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 他在英国受到的争议，几乎和在爱尔兰一样大。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a person that still opens up souls.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个至今仍能触动灵魂的人物。

sentences.en: I mean, we'll talk about the statue, but there's much more than that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们会谈到那座雕像，但远不止于此。

sentences.en: He's a deeply divisive character.
sentences.zh: 他是一个极具争议性的人物。

sentences.en: And I've been reminded of it just in the response to this book.
sentences.zh: 我从对这本书的反应中再次意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: But if we look at what happened in Ireland, it's – I think the key to the ruthlessness that Cromwell displays is something to do with this ruthlessness of the army
sentences.zh: 但如果我们看看爱尔兰发生了什么，它——我认为克伦威尔表现出的这种冷酷无情，与军队的冷酷无情有某种联系，

sentences.en: that takes place after the Second Civil War, when they're avenging blood, as they see it.
sentences.zh: 发生在第二次内战之后，当时他们正按照自己的理解在为血债复仇。

sentences.en: And the avenging blood in Ireland is the Irish Rebellion of 1641, which is exaggerated hugely at the time, but is real.
sentences.zh: 而在爱尔兰复仇的血债，就是1641年的爱尔兰起义，这件事在当时被极大地夸大了，但它确实发生了。

sentences.en: And it takes on the kind of propaganda in England.
sentences.zh: 并且它在英国演变成了一种宣传。

sentences.en: And I think the rebellion tells or signals to Protestants in England, the people who will fight Charles in the Civil War,
sentences.zh: 我认为这场起义向英国的新教徒——也就是在内战中与查理作战的人——发出了一个信号，

sentences.en: that the people over there are beyond the pale – sorry for the allusion there – but literally beyond the pale.
sentences.zh: 那就是海峡那边的人已经不可理喻了——抱歉借用了这个双关语——但字面意思确实是无法无天。

sentences.en: And therefore, it is time to settle Ireland once and for all.
sentences.zh: 因此，是时候一劳永逸地解决爱尔兰问题了。

sentences.en: So, Paul, by the standards of war as practised on the continent, is Cromwell's behaviour regarded as excessive even by that?
sentences.zh: 那么，保罗，按照当时欧洲大陆通行的战争标准来看，克伦威尔的行为甚至在那时也被视为过度吗？

sentences.en: Or is he behaving according to the accepted conventions of war?
sentences.zh: 还是说他的行为符合公认的战争惯例？

sentences.en: People behaved pretty badly in the Thirty Years' War, though, didn't they?
sentences.zh: 不过，在三十年战争中，人们的行为本来就很恶劣，对吧？

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然。

sentences.en: I mean, his defenders always say, well, you know, he was behaving according to the conventional standards.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他的辩护者总是说，你看，他当时的行为是符合传统标准的。

sentences.en: I mean, was he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: Well, let's have a look at – I mean, the only way you can really begin to answer this is looking at what happens.
sentences.zh: 嗯，让我们来看看——我的意思是，真正开始回答这个问题的唯一方法，就是看看当时究竟发生了什么。

sentences.en: James Butler, who's the Earl of Ormond, has brilliantly put together an Irish and Royalist coalition in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 奥蒙德伯爵詹姆斯·巴特勒在爱尔兰出色地组建了一个爱尔兰保王党联盟。

sentences.en: The aim being to secure Ireland as a base to attack England and to bring royalism back.
sentences.zh: 其目的是将爱尔兰作为进攻英国并恢复君主制的基地。

sentences.en: That's the kind of simple equation that he's dealing with.
sentences.zh: 这就是他所面临的简单局势。

sentences.en: And by about – he's got a strategy together by March 1649.
sentences.zh: 到大约——他在1649年3月前就制定好了一项战略。

sentences.en: So this is only two months after the king's been executed, if that.
sentences.zh: 所以这距离国王被处决仅仅过去了两个月，甚至更短。

sentences.en: He's got a campaign strategy together and appears to have the significant numbers to be able to take Dublin.
sentences.zh: 他制定好了战役战略，并且似乎拥有足够庞大的兵力来攻占都柏林。

sentences.en: And in fact, by the end of June, he's about two miles from Dublin.
sentences.zh: 事实上，到6月底，他已经推进到距离都柏林大约两英里远的地方。

sentences.en: Now, the decisive turning point here, I think, is that the defeat by Michael Jones at Rathmines of this royalist Irish force,
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为这里的决定性转折点是，迈克尔·琼斯在拉斯敏斯击溃了这支保王党爱尔兰军队，

sentences.en: that seems to me to be the decisive victory in this whole campaign.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这是整场战役的决定性胜利。

sentences.en: And that's the 2nd of August, because it allows – it stalls Ormond's campaign to want,
sentences.zh: 那是8月2日，因为这不仅阻挠了奥蒙德的攻势，

sentences.en: but it allows the new model army, 12,000 battle-hardened, theologically and ideologically primed
sentences.zh: 而且还将12000名经验丰富、经受过战火洗礼、在神学和意识形态上经过动员的英国士兵放入了都柏林，

sentences.en: and experienced British soldiers into Dublin, plus they have £100,000 in cash that's given them by Parliament.
sentences.zh: 此外他们还带着议会赠予的10万英镑现金。

sentences.en: So this is a serious force.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一支不容小觑的力量。

sentences.en: But it's also a force that goes into Ireland with Cromwell's firm instructions that any soldiers caught looting will be hanged.
sentences.zh: 但这也是一支带着克伦威尔严厉指示进入爱尔兰的军队，任何被抓到抢劫的士兵都会被绞死。

sentences.en: It goes in with a kind of core of discipline.
sentences.zh: 它带着一种核心纪律进入该地区。

sentences.en: And Drogheda is the place that's always mentioned.
sentences.zh: 德罗赫达是总是被提及的地方。

sentences.en: This is a significant town being fought over again and again by both sides.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重要的城镇，双方曾多次为之争夺。

sentences.en: The gateway to Ulster.
sentences.zh: 通往阿尔斯特的门户。

sentences.en: And Ormond appoints Arthur Ashton as the governor of this place.
sentences.zh: 奥蒙德任命阿瑟·阿什顿为这个地方的守城长官。

sentences.en: And when Cromwell emerges with his army to be sieges, he's offered the means to surrender.
sentences.zh: 当克伦威尔率领军队出现并进行围城时，他给对方提供了投降的途径。

sentences.en: Now, this is the normal process at this time.
sentences.zh: 在当时，这是正常流程。

sentences.en: It's seen endlessly in the Thirty Years' War.
sentences.zh: 这在三十年战争中屡见不鲜。

sentences.en: It's quite common elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 在其他地方也很常见。

sentences.en: If you offer the defenders the opportunity to surrender, they will be let go.
sentences.zh: 如果你给防守方提供投降的机会，他们就会被放走。

sentences.en: Ashton does not surrender.
sentences.zh: 阿什顿没有投降。

sentences.en: And his 2,500 men or other soldiers are there defending this.
sentences.zh: 他麾下的2500名士兵和其他官兵留下来进行防守。

sentences.en: And in the end, it falls to Cromwell's troops.
sentences.zh: 最后，这座城市落入了克伦威尔的军队手中。

sentences.en: Now, there are real atrocities there.
sentences.zh: 当时确实发生了真正的暴行。

sentences.en: The burning of St Peter's Church is particularly important.
sentences.zh: 圣彼得教堂被焚烧尤为严重。

sentences.en: There are people burned alive there.
sentences.zh: 有人在那里被活活烧死。

sentences.zh: 但我认为这是英国、英国与爱尔兰、欧洲，甚至全球历史上一个绝对至关重要的转折点，它对绝大多数英国人，甚至可能是爱尔兰人来说，

sentences.en: so far as the vast majority of British people go, perhaps even Irish people.
sentences.zh: 依然是一张白纸。

sentences.en: And it is something that I think really needs to be amended if we're to understand who we are.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想了解我们是谁，我认为这确实是需要改变的事情。

sentences.en: Paul, you often don't like modern parallels.
sentences.zh: 保罗，你通常不喜欢现代的类比。

sentences.en: And yet I read in your book an excellent modern parallel, which I heartily approve of, where at the end of your great book,
sentences.zh: 然而我在你的书中读到了一个非常出色的现代类比，我由衷地赞赏，在你这本伟大的书的结尾，

sentences.en: you say you draw a parallel between Cromwell and Margaret Thatcher, both East Anglians, non-conformists, you know, very decisive when they needed to be,
sentences.zh: 你说你将克伦威尔与玛格丽特·撒切尔进行了类比，两人都是东盎格利亚人、非国教徒，你知道的，在需要的时候非常果断，

sentences.en: very divisive, yeah, thought of as austere, but actually incredibly fun-loving.
sentences.zh: 非常具有分裂性，是的，被认为很简朴，但实际上极其热爱生活。

sentences.en: Do you think that...
sentences.zh: 你认为……

sentences.en: So talk to us about the Margaret Thatcher analogy, because I think that's one that most listeners will find extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 所以跟我们聊聊关于玛格丽特·撒切尔的类比吧，因为我认为大多数听众会觉得这非同寻常。

sentences.en: Well, I was being quite mischievous when I did this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我做这件事的时候其实挺淘气的。

sentences.en: Obviously, it is absolutely true that I don't like to draw modern parallels too closely, but I couldn't miss the Margaret Thatcher one because, you know, as you say,
sentences.zh: 显然，我的确不喜欢把现代类比拉得太近，但我不能错过玛格丽特·撒切尔这个类比，因为，你知道的，正如你所说，

sentences.en: there's this East Anglian non-conformist philo-semite.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个东盎格利亚的非国教徒兼亲犹太主义者。

sentences.en: We forget Cromwell's role in resettling Jews in England again.
sentences.zh: 我们忘记了克伦威尔在重新安置英国犹太人方面所起的作用。

sentences.en: Not that he did this for humanitarian purposes.
sentences.zh: 并不是说他这样做是为了人道主义目的。

sentences.en: He did it so that the Jews would convert to Protestantism, Christianity, in the most perfect of all Christian polities.
sentences.zh: 他这样做是为了让犹太人皈依新教、皈依基督教，融入最完美的基督教政体中。

sentences.en: But decisive in war, certainly.
sentences.zh: 但在战争中绝对是果断的。

sentences.en: Problem with the Irish, that's certainly there as well.
sentences.zh: 与爱尔兰人的问题，这当然也存在。

sentences.en: There are all kinds of parallels.
sentences.zh: 这里有各种各样的类比。

sentences.en: Now, what's been quite decisive, but I think the most interesting parallel of all,
sentences.zh: 现在，相当决定性的是，但我认为最有趣的类比是，

sentences.en: and we talked earlier about the Anglicisation of both Scotland and Ireland that was the plan of this,
sentences.zh: 我们之前讨论过苏格兰和爱尔兰的盎格利亚化，这是它的计划，

sentences.en: that I think in the end, even the English people disappointed Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 我认为最终，连英国人民都让克伦威尔失望了。

sentences.en: He described them, and I love this Cromwellian phrase, as under circumcision but raw.
sentences.zh: 他形容他们——我非常喜欢这个克伦威尔式的词汇——未受割礼但生嫩。

sentences.en: In other words, they were on a kind of path to a holiness, a perfection, but they weren't there yet, and indeed they were a long way off.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们正走在通往圣洁和完美的道路上，但他们还没走到，事实上还差得远呢。

sentences.en: And I think there was that kind of element with Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 我想撒切尔也有这种成分。

sentences.en: There's a wonderful phrase, I can't remember who did it, I don't know whether it was Vernon Bogdan or someone else, who said that Margaret Thatcher wanted to create a country
sentences.zh: 有一个绝妙的短语，我不记得是谁说的了，我不知道是弗农·博格丹还是别的什么人，他说玛格丽特·撒切尔想要建立一个国家，

sentences.en: in the image of her father, the Puritan Alderman Roberts, and created one in the image of her son.
sentences.zh: 这个国家带有她父亲——清教徒市参议员罗伯茨的影子，而她建立的国家却带着她儿子的影子。

sentences.en: And there's a kind of parallel with Cromwell, because who ultimately follows him?
sentences.zh: 这与克伦威尔有某种相似之处，因为最终谁继承了他？

sentences.en: For a brief while it's his son, but in the end it's Charles II.
sentences.zh: 短时间内是他的儿子，但最终是查理二世。

sentences.en: And there's this kind of inability to really read the desires of the English people.
sentences.zh: 这种无法真正揣摩英国人民愿望的情况是客观存在的。

sentences.en: So the English people, they'd let down Cromwell,
sentences.zh: 所以英国人民，他们让克伦威尔失望了，

sentences.en: they'd let down God, but worst of all, they'd let down themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们让上帝失望了，但最糟糕的是，他们让自己失望了。

sentences.en: So they let down me.
sentences.zh: 所以他们让我失望了。

sentences.en: And they let down Dominic.
sentences.zh: 他们让多米尼克失望了。

sentences.en: On that note, we're going to bid you adieu to thank Paul.
sentences.zh: 就此而言，我们要向保罗道别并表达感谢。

sentences.en: He was lamenting
sentences.zh: 他一直在感叹

sentences.en: the fact that people don't know much about Cromwell or what they know about him is largely mythic.
sentences.zh: 人们对克伦威尔知之甚少，或者他们所知道的基本上都是神话。

sentences.en: To get around that problem, I do recommend buying his wonderful book,
sentences.zh: 为了解决这个问题，我强烈建议购买他的好书，

sentences.en: Providence Lost,
sentences.zh: 《失去的普罗维登斯：

sentences.en: The Rise and Fall of Cromwell's Protectorate.
sentences.zh: 克伦威尔护国公政体的兴衰》。

sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.zh: 我们下周再见。
